text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- It is possible that Estonia will be accepted into the EU in the first round, German ambassador Bernd Muetzelburg said at a conference "Estonia and the EU".
- An Estonian-Finnish agreement on the return of illegal immigrants came into force yesterday.

- More than 70 forged documents proving proficiency in the Estonian language have been presented by people applying for Estonain citizenship. Knowledge of Estonian is a key part of the naturalisation procedure for Russians in Estonia.
- 15 police officers have been dismissed so far in 1996 for taking bribes and drinking on duty, the director of the police department said.
- The government has simplified rules for land privatisation, a survey of the land will not be needed if a detailed map exists.
- Estonia's EU entry is hampered by its unsolved border dispute with Russia and the situation of its Russian minority. Foreign Minister Siim Kallas said.
- Writers Jaan Kross and Jaan Kaplinski did not succeed in winning the 1996 Nobel literature prize.
